source.title: Grokking, Rank Minimization and Generalization in Deep Learning
source.authors: David Yunis; Kumar Kshitij Patel; Samuel Wheeler; P. Savarese; Gal Vardi; Karen Livescu; Michael Maire; Matthew R. Walter

record.tranche_reason: Trains an MLP on true and random CIFAR-10 labels, echoing the random-label memorization test, and measures training and validation error plus rank properties.
record.gate_note: The random-label experiment reports zero training error for both label conditions. Validation error is shown in Figure 8 but not described in text; rank and alignment measurements are relevant findings but do not themselves measure the version's generalization claim.
record.test_reason: Section 6 repeats the CIFAR-10 true-label versus random-label experiment with an MLP, measuring training and validation error. The constant learning rate changes the recipe but preserves the method and measures relevant to V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label experiment, but is narrower than the paper's conclusion: generalization during grokking coincides with low-rank solutions, rank reduction occurs across practical tasks, weight decay promotes it, and true-label versus random-label fits differ in rank. The authors offer these observations as evidence toward understanding generalization, without a comprehensive explanatory theory.
record.recipe_differences: The study revisits the random-label memorization experiment on CIFAR-10 with a 4-layer MLP, using constant learning rate 0.001 rather than the learning-rate schedule attributed to Zhang et al. (2021).
record.method_sensitivity: The label condition (true versus random) changes the reported effective-rank and alignment behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: True-label training produces lower middle-layer effective rank and persistent alignment; random-label alignment appears and later disappears.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: True-label and random-label fits differ in effective rank and alignment dynamics in a four-layer CIFAR-10 MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: Generalization during grokking coincides with low-rank weights, and weight decay promotes effective-rank reduction across several architectures and tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral dynamics and weight decay are associated with low-rank solutions; these results do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness.

record.problems: Only 3 random seeds were used. Validation-error outcomes relevant to V1 are presented as a figure without a textual description or recoverable values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No results left out; the reported rank and alignment findings do not measure a claim version and are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Other architectures and ImageNet are not tested. Natural-label held-out accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance are measured in Figure 8 but cannot be determined from the supplied text.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond interpolation.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Separate training-error rows for true and completely random labels: Section 6 explicitly reports zero training error in both conditions. These establish the fitting component of V1 and should not be classified solely as an unrelated rank finding.

record.verdict_notes: No directional verdict on V1 is justified from the supplied text: zero training error in both label conditions establishes fitting capacity, but the unreadable validation curves prevent establishing the claimed coexistence with generalization. The study is not an original source for V1.

versions.untested_parts: Exact held-out accuracy relative to chance is not stated; validation error appears only in Figure 8 without a textual description. The study tests a 4-layer MLP only, not the listed architectures or ImageNet setting.
